- **self**: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics (15/3)

## Structure and components

- [statement] Atlas preserves the existing IOPS rate when switching from Gen1 to Gen2, so retained IOPS above the new included baseline can become a separately billed component; the generation switch alone does not establish savings. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/storage.md · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs.md

## How it works

- [statement] AWS gp3 independently prices performance beyond an included 3,000-IOPS baseline and supports performance scaling without buying more capacity. This corroborates the underlying economic mechanism, but AWS's native disk pricing and baseline rules are not an Atlas price quote: Atlas documents its own capacity-dependent baseline and separate charges. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Atlas Gen2 storage charges include baseline IOPS. The documented baseline is 3,000 IOPS through 1,000 GB and scales at three IOPS per GB above that; examples include 6,000 IOPS at 2,000 GB and 12,000 at 4,000 GB. Atlas bills Extended Standard IOPS beyond the included baseline separately from storage capacity. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs.md
- [statement] In a September 26, 2026 firsthand account, Jayabal Rajendran, identifying himself as InsuredMine's Director of Engineering, reported provisioning 12,000 IOPS with 1 TB on Gen2 and reducing I/O wait from roughly 50% to below 3%. The combined change also reduced the cluster from M80 to M50; it does not isolate Gen2's contribution or establish a general savings percentage. (low confidence) — https://medium.com/@devloprjayabal/how-atlas-gen2-cut-our-iops-wait-from-50-to-3-and-halved-our-cluster-size-e458d3f2b4ca · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics
- [statement] MongoDB's Gen2 announcement reports an internal pilot with 15–20% lower CPU utilization and approximately 45% lower read/write latency. These are vendor-observed pilot outcomes, not an independently reproduced benchmark, an invoice reduction, or a guaranteed improvement for a migration workload. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-10) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-atlas-gen2-on-aws-m30-dedicated-clusters · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics
- [statement] The documented Gen2 standard baseline is 3,000 IOPS through 1,000 GB, then three IOPS per GB: 2,000 GB includes 6,000 IOPS and 4,000 GB includes 12,000 IOPS. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Jayabal Rajendran, whose author biography identifies him with InsuredMine, reports provisioning 12,000 IOPS on Gen2 and a reduction in IOPS wait from roughly 50% to under 3%; the article describes simultaneous compute/storage changes, lacks a before/after invoice, and cannot isolate Gen2-only cost savings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-26) — https://medium.com/@devloprjayabal/how-atlas-gen2-cut-our-iops-wait-from-50-to-3-and-halved-our-cluster-size-e458d3f2b4ca · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Eligible M30+ Gen2 dedicated clusters on AWS and Google Cloud allow Standard IOPS and storage capacity to scale independently. This provides a way to meet I/O demand without purchasing extra storage solely to obtain more IOPS; it is an optimization opportunity rather than a guaranteed reduction in migration cost. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/storage.md
- [statement] Cost estimation should compare the Atlas builder quote for generation, storage capacity, IOPS type and IOPS rate; derive the chargeable Extended Standard component from provisioned IOPS above the storage-linked baseline, rather than importing a raw AWS dollar-per-IOPS price as an Atlas quote (methodological inference). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/storage.md · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Changing from Gen1 to Gen2 preserves the existing IOPS rate; on AWS it also preserves the storage-performance category, mapping Provisioned IOPS to High Performance IOPS. Retained IOPS can exceed the baseline bundled with Gen2 storage, so changing generation alone does not establish that the bill will fall. Atlas recommends estimating the proposed configuration in its cluster builder. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/storage.md · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs.md
- [statement] Extended Standard IOPS has documented maximums of 80,000 on AWS Gen2 and 160,000 on Google Cloud Gen2. These are product ceilings, not a promise that every cluster tier or workload can sustain that rate. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/storage.md
- [statement] On AWS, Standard IOPS uses General Purpose SSD while High Performance IOPS uses Provisioned IOPS SSD. MongoDB warns that their latency and consistency characteristics differ; AWS independently recommends io2 Block Express for latency-sensitive workloads. Matching a numeric IOPS setting therefore does not establish performance equivalence, and changing IOPS type requires workload testing. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/storage.md · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics · also: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html
- [statement] Atlas includes a baseline IOPS allowance in Gen2 storage charges and bills Extended Standard IOPS above that allowance separately; independent provisioning does not mean free additional performance. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs.md
- [statement] On AWS, Atlas preserves the IOPS class during a generation change: Gen1 Provisioned IOPS becomes Gen2 High Performance IOPS, while standard remains standard; MongoDB recommends changing generation and IOPS type separately and checking performance between changes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/storage.md · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics
- [statement] MongoDB markets Gen2 as an infrastructure upgrade retaining Atlas APIs, connection strings and operational model without application rearchitecture; its FAQ describes the generation switch as a cluster-tier change. For an existing eligible Atlas deployment, evaluate this path before assuming an external data migration is required. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-10) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-atlas-gen2-on-aws-m30-dedicated-clusters · keywords: Gen2 clusters and Extended Standard IOPS economics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/storage.md
